prerequisites: Basic laws of electricity (Gauss's law, Maxwell's laws)
Basics of quantum physics (quantization of energy levels in atoms, band structure of solids)
Operation of an electrical circuit (consisting of voltage or current sources, resistors, capacitors)
Small-signal analysis of an electrical circuit

learning_outcomes.text: Acquire knowledge of the basic operation and properties of the main semiconductor components important for both electronics, electrical energy, and nanotechnology engineers.
Understand the physical operation of components.
Be able to set up models for semiconductor components.
Become familiar with the fabrication process of semiconductor components.

syllabus_topics: Equilibrium and non-equilibrium: recombination and generation mechanisms
Current behavior and I-V characteristics for ideal diffusion operation
Non-ideal operation: recombination, generation, breakdown, high injection
The MOS capacitor: 3 operating regions and C-V characteristics
Operation of the MOS transistor: accumulation, depletion, inversion
Current-voltage characteristics: linear and saturation regions
The MOS transistor as amplifier and switch
The CMOS inverter: power consumption and time delay
Non-idealities: emitter efficiency and base transport factor
Different operating regions: forward active, inverse active, cutoff, saturation
The bipolar transistor as amplifier and switch

assessment_methods.method: Written exam during the examination period
Three interim written evaluations during the semester

assessment_rules: The final score is composed of a written exam (90%) and three interim written evaluations (10%). If a student is absent for one or two interim evaluations with a valid reason, the remaining scores count proportionally (e.g., one test counts for 5%). If no interim tests are taken for a valid reason, the exam counts for 100%. For students scoring 18/20 or more on the June exam, the interim tests only count if they increase the final score. A final score between 9.50/20 and 9.99/20 will be rounded to 9/20. If a student scores 0 on a major exercise in the exam, the final score will be capped at 10/20. For resits, the re-examination score counts for 100% of the final score; interim evaluation scores are not considered.
institution: KU Leuven - Faculty of Engineering Science
degree: Bachelor in de ingenieurswetenschappen (Bachelor of Engineering Science, Leuven)
